AC: Given one existing ticket whose Id starts with hex prefix P, 'todo.py search P' includes that ticket in its results even when P shares no lexical/semantic overlap with any Summary/Body text. A P matching zero or more than one ticket falls back to ordinary ranked search only (no error, no spurious single match). Multi-term queries never engage the prefix path. The web viewer's search box (/search?q=P) shows the same behavior, since it is backed by the same search_tickets/run_search functions as the CLI command.
ActualSummary: Added a solo-term hex-id-prefix search strategy (pins a unique Id-prefix hit first, shared by CLI search and the web viewer's search box), plus a small visible objid badge on every objid-bearing box/section in the web viewer (work items, subtodos, parents, Summary/Body/LongSummary, generic Fields rows) so a permalink's objid can be read straight off the page.

Body.raw:
search_tickets (skills/projectmanagement/todos/todo.py:1778), reached via the shared run_search (todo.py:5425), ranks by reciprocal-rank fusion over vector embedders plus one lexical IDF ranking -- it treats every query term as ordinary text to embed/match. Both consumers of run_search go through this same path: the 'search' CLI command (SearchCommand, todo.py:5453) and the web viewer's search box (WebCommand.search_rows, todo.py:5243, backing the /search route in todo_web.py used by the bare 'web' base page). Neither special-cases a query that looks like an Id prefix, even though resolve_ticket_by_id (todo.py:1612) already implements exactly that 4+ hex prefix match for direct selectors elsewhere (get, set, web ?id=, etc.) -- so pasting a short id prefix into search does not reliably find the ticket it names, since a hex string has no lexical/semantic overlap with Summary/Body text.

Add a search strategy: when a search invocation has exactly one term, additionally attempt that term as a hex prefix against every ticket's Id (same prefix-matching semantics as resolve_ticket_by_id), and fold any hit into the results alongside the normal ranked search. Multi-term queries are unaffected -- the prefix attempt only applies to the solo-term case. Implementing this once in the shared search_tickets/run_search path covers both the CLI 'search' command and the web base page's search box without duplicating logic.

Summary.raw: Search: try a solo query term as a todo id prefix

WorkItems.message:
todo search: pin a unique solo-term id-prefix hit first

search_tickets/run_search fused vector+lexical rankers over query terms with
no id awareness, so a bare hex id prefix (no lexical/semantic overlap with
Summary/Body text) could not reliably find its ticket even though the same
prefix works everywhere else (resolve_ticket_by_id).

Add _solo_term_id_prefix_hit: for a single search term shaped like a 4+ hex
selector, uniquely matched against every candidate ticket's Id, pinned first
in the results. Zero or ambiguous matches fall back to ordinary ranked search
untouched; multi-term queries never engage the path. Covers both the CLI
'search' command and the web viewer's search box, which share this function.

WorkItems.message:
todo web: show each object's own objid, small and visible

Work item, subtodo and parent boxes, plus Summary/Body/LongSummary sections and
generic Fields rows, already carry an objid internally (_box_attrs /
_section_attrs stamp it as the DOM anchor and permalink scroll target) but
never showed it -- reading a permalink's objid off the page required
inspecting the DOM.

Add _objid_badge/_first_objid and wire them into _wi_box, _st_box,
_parent_box (absolute-positioned corner label) and _section()'s heading plus
_meta_html's per-row heading (inline label). A list-shaped section (Work
items, Subtodos, Parent) has no objid of its own -- only its elements do, and
those already show theirs. Static fold reprs stay plain, same scope as
_box_attrs.
WorkItems.summary: Web viewer: render each object's objid visibly, small in a corner of its box -- work item and subtodo boxes (_wi_box/_st_box, todo_web.py:372,422), parent boxes (_parents_html, todo_web.py:498), and the top-level sections (Summary/Body/LongSummary/WorkItems/Subtodos, _section_attrs, todo_web.py:312) that already carry an objid via _box_attrs/_section_attrs but only expose it as a data-obj attribute today, not as visible text. Purely cosmetic/debug aid so a permalink's objid (/<todoid>/objid/<objid>) can be read straight off the page instead of only via right-click/inspect.
